issues.failure_explanation: The displayed bound pairs the pointwise quantity -log q_theta(u_0|a) with a right-hand side that averages over u_0 ~ p(u_0|a) and is therefore constant in u_0. The derivation in Appendix 'Decomposition of the conditional VLB' starts from the identity log q_theta(u_0|a) = E_{p(u_0|a)}[log q_theta(u_0|a)], which is false whenever u_0|a is not a Dirac measure (e.g., for the Gaussian-noise data u_eta = u + eta the paper explicitly considers); Jensen therefore bounds only the averaged NLL, not the pointwise NLL. The same defect appears in the unconditional bound of Section 3.1. What is established is E_{p(u_0|a)}[-log q_theta(u_0|a)] <= -VLB, not the stated pointwise inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Move the expectation over u_0 to the left-hand side of the bound and remove the false first equality in Appendix B.1; all results and guarantees are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed pointwise variational bound on the conditional log-likelihood is not established; only the averaged bound used for training is supported.
issues.title: Conditional VLB stated as a pointwise bound but derived only in averaged form
issues.why_classification: A local re-pairing of one displayed inequality (and one false equality in the appendix) repairs it; no rate, guarantee, or algorithmic content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
We evaluate 
the prediction accuracy and uncertainty of the model $\SOPA$ 
by the mean relative $L_2$-error (MRLE) and the mean standard deviation (MSTD) that are defined by
\# of samples $N_s$   &  $1$ if noise-free; $100$ if noisy

issues.failure_explanation: MSTD is introduced as the metric evaluating 'the uncertainty of the model', but it is defined as the test-set average of ||std({S_theta^(n)(a)})||_2 divided by N_s. The sample standard deviation itself estimates the spread of the learned conditional distribution and does not vanish as N_s grows, so dividing by N_s makes the reported value decay like 1/N_s for any fixed model and be incomparable across choices of N_s; it is neither the conditional standard deviation (no division) nor the standard error of the mean (which requires 1/sqrt(N_s)). Moreover, in the noise-free setting of every reported table N_s = 1, for which the formula gives exactly 0 (or is undefined with Bessel's correction), while the tables report nonzero values (e.g., 5.08e-07), so the reported numbers cannot follow from the stated definition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the 1/N_s factor (report the mean per-gridpoint sample standard deviation) or replace it by 1/sqrt(N_s) if the standard error of the sample mean is intended, and recompute or relabel the reported values; no qualitative conclusion changes.
issues.overall_effect: The MSTD values in Tables 1-3 and the advertised uncertainty evaluation via MSTD are not produced by the stated formula and do not estimate the model's output uncertainty; the MRLE definition and the accuracy comparisons are unaffected.
issues.title: MSTD metric divides the standard deviation by the number of samples and cannot measure model uncertainty
issues.why_classification: Fixing one normalization constant repairs the estimator; no theorem, guarantee, or experimental conclusion of the paper depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed chain is asserted to hold 'in both cases'. In the noise-free case the initial state is Dirac (as assumed in Proposition prop:added-1), so the law of (u_0,...,u_T) is singular: it has no Lebesgue density, the quantity E_p[-log p(u_{0:T})] is undefined/infinite, while the middle expression H_p(u_T) + sum_t H_p(u_{t-1}|u_t) is finite; in addition H_p(u_T) = (n/2) log(2*pi*e*(1-alpha_bar_T)) differs from H_{q_theta}(u_T) = (n/2) log(2*pi*e), so the middle equality also fails. Even in the Gaussian-noise case, where the displayed entropies do match, equality of self-entropies does not show that q_theta 'achieves the exact likelihood under the true model p', which would require matching the cross-entropy, i.e., also the reverse means.
